=Analyze the "body" of each message in the provided conversation and arrange them in chronological order. Use the following format for the output:

[Timestamp] - [Sender]: [Message body]

For example:
12:01 pm - Customer: this is a test message
12:05 pm - Sales: this is a test reply

Instructions:
Only use the "body" of each message to construct the conversation.
Ensure the messages are ordered chronologically based on their timestamps.
Return the output in the exact format shown above.
If no conversation is found, return exactly: "No conversation found."

This is the conversation that needs conversion:
{{ $('Code').item.json.conversations }}

=Analyze the last customer message and the conversation history to determine if the customer is asking a vehicle-related questions or wants to know about a specific vehicle. Follow these exact rules:

Return "true" if any of the following conditions are met:
The last message mentions specific vehicle details (e.g., make, model, year, price, features).
The last message asks about the availability of a specific vehicle.
The conversation history shows an ongoing discussion about a specific vehicle.
The last message includes questions about vehicle specifications, condition, or pricing.

Return "false" if any of the following conditions are met:
The message is about general dealership information (e.g., hours, location, contact info).
The message is about service, maintenance, or repairs.
The message is a scheduling request (e.g., appointments, test drives, service bookings).
The message asks generic availability questions without mentioning specific vehicles.
The message is about warranty or financing without specific vehicle context.
The message is a general greeting or small talk.
The message mentions the customer’s location or plans to visit the dealership.

Examples where you should return "true":
"Do you have any Honda Civics in stock?"
"What's the mileage on that 2019 Ford F-150?"
"Is the black Toyota Camry still available?"
"How much is the Mercedes C300?"
"Do you have the stock number 21956?"

Examples where you should return "false":
"What are your business hours?"
"Can I schedule a test drive?"
"What's your phone number?"
"I would like to come by and test drive at 10 am tomorrow."

This is the last customer message sent:
{{ $node['Webhook'].json.body.customData.lastmessage }}

For context, here is the conversation history:
{{ $json.output }}

Respond with exactly "true" or "false" without any additional text.

=You are an automotive expert. Identify if the customer is providing you the year, make, model or stock number.

If the customer provided you the year, make or model, your output should be "YMM".

If it is stock number it should be "STOCK".

your response is used in an automation, so it is important to only respond with the information needed.

An example of year, make or model is: 2020 Ford Expedition

An example of stock numbers are:
- 12548
- 12548CO
- TI12548

=Analyze and Identify if the customer is booking for an appointment or general inquiry.

If the customer is booking for an appointment, your output should be "book".

If not, your output should be "general".

Your response is used in an automation, make sure to only respond what is relevant.

You can refer to the conversation here:
 {{ $('Format Message').item.json.output }}

=Analyze and identify if the customer wants to book an appointment. It is crucial to check between the last customer message and the conversation to identify what the customer wants.

If you see the time and date, your output should be in ISO 8601 format in Easter Timezone.

If you see no appointment date and time, or it is out of business hours, the response is null.

Customers will be setting up an appointment in the future or the same day, make sure to verify the date first before booking.

Our business hours in Eastern Timezone are:
Monday to Friday 10 am to 8 pm. Saturday at 9 am to 8 pm. And Sunday from 12 noon to 6 pm.

For context, this is current time: {{$now}} - Convert in Eastern Timezone.

Your response is being used in an automation, reply with only the formatted date and time no extra words or comments.
